tagline: Thirteen one-way miles under cliffs where old rock rides on young.
intro: The loop leaves the visitor center going one way only, a moderate climb at first and then mostly downhill or flat for 13 miles. Side roads and pullouts reach the trailheads below walls of red and cream sandstone as much as 3,000 feet high.

The mix of colors is the work of the Keystone Thrust, which pushed older gray rock over the younger red, and the seam shows along the escarpment for 13 miles. Near the north end of the loop the Excelsior Company once quarried the sandstone, found it did not pay, and left some of the huge blocks behind.
season: BLM suggests the warmer months, for better views and more daylight on the drive.

moments.title: Red Rock Canyon Visitor Center
moments.text: The loop starts here, beside a habitat for the desert tortoise that houses eight females and two males.

moments.title: Bridge Mountain
moments.text: From Willow Springs hikers walk 5 miles to the summit, by way of a sandstone arch, the leftover side of an eroded rock water tank. Ponderosa pines hide in a cleft at the top.

practical: From October 1 to May 31, entry between 8 am and 5 pm requires a timed entry reservation for each day.
